newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's FNK wins 51 pct of oil group Sibneft.
newsitem.headline: Russia's FNK wins 51 pct of oil group Sibneft.

text.p: OOO Finansovaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (FNK), a hitherto unknown oil industry investment vehicle, won a 51 percent stake in Russia's seventh biggest oil producer Sibneft at an investment tender on Monday, the organiser of the tender, Neftyana Finansovaya Kompaniya (NFK), said.

Officials at NFK, which is controlled by Russian businessman and presidential confidant Boris Berezovsky, and which had managed the stake since late 1995 on behalf of the government, declined to comment on whether there was any relationship between NFK and FNK.

FNK won the tender for 51 percent of OAO Sibirskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sibneft) with a bid of $110 million. The starting price was $101 million. The successful bidder must also invest about $100 million in Sibneft. NFK had won the right to manage the stake under the government's shares-for-loans scheme with a $100.3 million credit to the government.

A senior official from Russia's third biggest bank Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian) said a bid from her bank, and another bid from another major bank, Alfa-Bank, had been rejected for not meeting the tender's conditions.

Uneximbank deputy chairman Yekaterina Voronova told reporters that four bids had been accepted, including one from regional oil group KomiTEK, and one from the hitherto unknown ZAO Kopf. Foreigners were excluded.
Sibneft's main production unit is Noyabrskneftegaz.
